content.text: You are a carpenter who hangs screens in movie theaters. You want to turn the pages of the "4K UHD Monitor User Manual" into a set of luggage checklists that "turn the monitor manual into a theater construction kit: mounting nails, signal ropes, power supply, picture panel and troubleshooting ladder." Each subsequent round must follow the box locations, packing order and no-mixing rules of the first round.
Please read these pages in order:

.

Now don't think of them as a book of information that you can just flip through, but as a set of segmented scripts that must be implemented on the spot. You need to create a box location first, and the fields are fixed as: hanger nails, signal ropes, power fires, screen panels, and troubleshooting ladders. All pages or consecutive page segments that enter the same column must meet three things at the same time: first, they answer the same type of on-site questions; second, they serve the same group of roles or at the same point in time; third, they lack roughly the same prerequisites. As long as one of them changes significantly, they cannot be merged into the same column for the sake of convenience.

The first round must be registered page by page or page by page. Each entry should at least include: which box position this page belongs to, whether it is more suitable for "packing" or "unpacking" or "no mixing", what should be established before it at least, where can it be followed at most, and if someone moves it forward or backward, what type of things will be changed first - objects, conditions, time points, roles, costs, permissions, resources, or completion status. You also need to assign at least one "gatekeeper page" to each slot: without it, the column can easily be said to be wider or narrower.There are four additional results to hand in this round. First, give the most stable main line, which requires that you can start from the overview or entrance page, actually go to a more specific landing point, and then return to the conditions, ending or supplementary page. Second, give a sub-line that seems reasonable but will cause misalignment once it is put into the scene, and clearly write down where the first misalignment occurs. Third, provide a "suspension area", including at least two pages or two page segments, explaining why they cannot enter the main line now, but they should not be deleted. Fourth, a set of "adjacent pages that cannot be separated" and a set of "pages that cannot be combined because they are adjacent" are given. These four items must be explained by referring to the information visible in the "4K UHD Monitor User Manual" itself. You cannot rely on outside common sense to complete it for you.

rubrics: 1. The response should cover all pages or page segments, and pack each page into one of the `rack nails`, `signal rope`, `power fire`, `screen tray`, and `troubleshooting ladder`; the reason for packing must be "Which step of the hands-on problem does this page solve, what kind of pre-state does it rely on, and what will go wrong if it is advanced." You cannot just look at the appearance or title of the device.

2. The response should also separate the responsibilities of the `rack nail`, `signal rope`, `power fire`, `screen panel` and `troubleshooting ladder`: the physical/opening page that can be directly used, the page that will change the connection or power supply status, the page that describes the output and setting results, and the page that is only safely activated in case of exception or after-sales service, cannot steal each other's positions.

3. The response should the main line must reflect the dependence of "first create the object - then change the state - then confirm the result - and finally handle the exception/after-sales service"; if the `screen disk' is used as the unboxing entrance, or the `troubleshooting ladder' is used as daily steps instead of exception review, remediation or closure, this must not be done.

4. The response should the gatekeeping page must be able to explain which two box positions it will confuse if missing, such as confusing `signal rope` and `power supply fire` as the same type of connection, or mistaking `hanger nail` and `inspection ladder` as entrance instructions; it cannot just say "it is the most critical".

5. The response should also explain: If the page segment boundaries are used in different ways, the packing order, status changes, and exception pages must not be preceded must still be maintained; if it is just to pack adjacent pages more tightly, as long as the dependencies are not changed.

6. The response should not directly mention the catalog, overview, warranty, version differences, troubleshooting or after-sales information as the first hands-on step, or combine the `signal rope`, `power supply` and `screen panel` into one box just because the same equipment diagram appears.
